IF YOU WANT TO BECOME A SENIOR ENGINEER FASTER, STOP COUNTING YEARS.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 LEVERS:

Own outcomes, not tickets.

Juniors close tasks. Seniors move metrics. Ask what number your work changes.

Write the doc nobody wants to write.

Design docs, runbooks, postmortems. Visibility compounds faster than commits.

Delete code on purpose.

Every quarter, kill something: a flag, a service, dead code. Simplifiers get promoted.

I post daily breakdowns like this for backend, SQL, and interviews.

Follow @owlsky17 so you don't miss the next one.
THINGS THAT QUIETLY KILL ENGINEERING CAREERS:

Never asking questions.

Silent confusion ships bugs. The fastest engineers ask the dumb question on day one.

Avoiding code review feedback.

Defensiveness freezes growth. Treat every comment as free mentoring.

Staying comfortable one level too long.

If you are the expert in every room, you are in the wrong rooms.

IF YOU WANT YOUR SIDE PROJECT TO SURVIVE, STOP ADDING FEATURES.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 RULES:

Ship to one user first.

Yourself counts. Real usage teaches more than ten planned features.

Boring tech wins weekends.

Monolith, Postgres, one host. Excitement is for work hours.

Log progress in public.

Weekly demos beat yearly launches. Accountability ships products.
